Ticket #195415 (flutter/flutter, "[gestures] latestPointer switches control to a stationary second finger when the first finger starts a drag") is labeled P2 ("P2 Important issues not at the top of the work list"); it also carries f: gestures, framework, has reproducible steps, team-framework, and triaged-framework, and is assigned to Renzo-Olivares.

What is broken: with MultitouchDragStrategy.latestPointer, when a second finger goes down inside the drag area before either finger moves, the stationary second pointer becomes the active pointer and takes over the drag. Per the reporter and mbcorona's confirmation, acceptGesture adds each accepted pointer to _acceptedActivePointers and sets _activePointer = pointer (monodrag.dart lines 738-741), so pointer 2 becomes active even though it never moved; the latestPointer move filter (monodrag.dart lines 456-457: `result = _activePointer == null || pointer == _activePointer;`) then drops subsequent move events from pointer 1. Observed behavior: finger 1 crosses the drag threshold and emits drag START, but its further movement produces no onUpdate callbacks while finger 2 is down; moving finger 2 produces updates, and only after finger 2 is lifted can finger 1 drive updates again — the drag looks like it stops responding right after it starts. The logs in the report show exactly this: raw MOVE p5 events with no drag UPDATE between acceptGesture(p6) ENTER at line 181 and raw UP p6 at line 248, followed by drag UPDATE from p5 resuming at lines 250+. The open question flagged by mbcorona is whether latestPointer should hand control to a pointer that never moved (the report presents this as a proposed interaction expectation, not a claim of contradicting documented API behavior).

What is broken: when a drag recognizer is configured with MultitouchDragStrategy.latestPointer and a second finger goes down before the drag threshold is exceeded (a competing tap recognizer keeps the arena contested), the drag starts from finger 1 but then stops producing onUpdate callbacks for finger 1 while the stationary finger 2 remains down — moving finger 2 produces updates instead, and finger 1 only drives updates again after finger 2 is lifted. Flutter issue #195415 — "[gestures] latestPointer switches control to a stationary second finger when the first finger starts a drag" (opened by @Pancf, ~20h ago; assigned to Renzo-Olivares, team-framework).

What is broken: With MultitouchDragStrategy.latestPointer, when finger 1 is held down and finger 2 is put down before either moves, moving finger 1 past the drag threshold correctly emits drag START — but then finger 1's continued movement produces no onUpdate callbacks. Updates only resume from finger 2 (which never moved), and finger 1 regains control only after finger 2 is lifted. The drag looks like it freezes right after starting even though the initiating finger is still moving.

Cause per maintainer @mbcorona: crossing the threshold calls resolve(GestureDisposition.accepted) for the recognizer's pending pointers, and acceptGesture(pointer) sets _activePointer = pointer on each acceptance (monodrag.dart lines ~738–741). Pointer 2 is accepted right after pointer 1, so the stationary pointer 2 becomes _activePointer, and the latestPointer filter (case MultitouchDragStrategy.latestPointer: result = _activePointer == null || pointer == _activePointer, monodrag.dart ~456–457) then excludes pointer 1's move events via _shouldTrackMoveEvent.

Reproduction logs included in the report: "drag START" followed by acceptGesture(p5)/acceptGesture(p6), raw MOVE p5 events with no corresponding drag UPDATE, then "drag UPDATE from p6" once finger 2 moves, and drag UPDATE from p5 again after "raw UP p6".

Expected: the finger whose movement started the drag should keep producing drag updates while it remains down. The reporter frames this as a proposed interaction expectation and asks whether this pre-acceptance multi-pointer handoff is intentional; if so, it should be documented.

Labels: P2, f: gestures, framework, has reproducible steps, team-framework, triaged-framework. No type, project, milestone, or linked PRs.

Issue #195415 "[gestures] latestPointer switches control to a stationary second finger when the first finger starts a drag" carries the label "P2 Important issues not at the top of the work list" (also labeled f: gestures, framework, has reproducible steps, team-framework, triaged-framework; assigned to Renzo-Olivares).

What is broken: In Flutter's monodrag gesture recognizer with MultitouchDragStrategy.latestPointer, when two fingers are down (finger 1 then finger 2, with finger 2 stationary) and finger 1's movement crosses the drag threshold, the drag START fires but subsequent movement of finger 1 produces no onUpdate callbacks — the drag appears to freeze right after it starts. Only moving the second (previously stationary) finger produces updates, and after finger 2 is lifted, finger 1 drives updates again.

Root cause as explained in the report and confirmed by mbcorona: crossing the threshold calls resolve(GestureDisposition.accepted) for the pending pointers, and acceptGesture(pointer) sets _activePointer = pointer on each acceptance (monodrag.dart lines 738-741). When pointer 1 and then pointer 2 are accepted, stationary pointer 2 becomes the active pointer, and _shouldTrackMoveEvent (monodrag.dart lines 456-457, `result = _activePointer == null || pointer == _activePointer;`) then filters out pointer 1's move events.

Reported expectation: the finger whose movement started the drag should keep producing drag updates while it stays down. The open question raised is whether latestPointer should hand control to a pointer that never moved; if the behavior is intentional, documenting this case is requested. Reproduced via a code sample with logs showing acceptGesture(p5)/acceptGesture(p6) and updates switching to p6.

Ticket flutter/flutter#195415 — "[gestures] latestPointer switches control to a stationary second finger when the first finger starts a drag" (opened by Pancf, ~20h ago; labels include P2, f: gestures, framework, has reproducible steps, team-framework, triaged-framework; assigned to Renzo-Olivares).

Priority: P2 ("Important issues not at the top of the work list").

What is broken: When a HorizontalDragGestureRecognizer uses MultitouchDragStrategy.latestPointer, the second pointer to be accepted takes over the drag even if it has never moved. Repro: finger 1 goes down, finger 2 goes down and stays stationary inside the same area, finger 1 then moves past the drag slop so `drag START` is emitted. At that point crossing the threshold calls `resolve(GestureDisposition.accepted)` for the recognizer's pending pointers, and `acceptGesture(pointer)` sets `_activePointer = pointer` on each acceptance, so pointer 2 becomes active despite not having moved. `_shouldTrackMoveEvent` (case MultitouchDragStrategy.latestPointer: `result = _activePointer == null || pointer == _activePointer;`) then filters out pointer 1's subsequent move events.

Actual result: finger 1 initiated the drag but its continued movement produces no onUpdate callbacks while finger 2 is down; only moving finger 2 produces drag updates, and after finger 2 lifts, finger 1 drives updates again — the drag appears to stop responding right after it starts. Logs confirm this: after `drag START` and `acceptGesture(p6)`, raw MOVE p5 events yield no `drag UPDATE`, while raw MOVE p6 yields `drag UPDATE from p6`; after `raw UP p6` the updates resume from p5.

Expected: the finger whose movement started the drag should keep producing drag updates while it remains down, without requiring movement of a different, stationary finger. Reporter frames this as a proposed interaction expectation and asks whether the pre-acceptance multi-pointer handoff is intentional, and to document it if so. Flutter maintainer mbcorona confirmed the mechanism (acceptGesture making each accepted pointer active + latestPointer move filter tracking only that pointer) and routed it to team-framework, noting the open question is whether latestPointer should hand control to a pointer that never moved. Environment: Flutter 3.50.0-0.2.pre, channel master, darwin-arm64.

Issue #195397 ("TableBorder.lerp and TableBorder.scale drop borderRadius") is a P2 ("Important issues not at the top of the work list") framework bug owned by team-framework. What's broken: TableBorder.lerp(a, b, 0.5) and b.scale(0.5) both return BorderRadius.zero instead of interpolating/scaling the radius (expected BorderRadius.circular(8) and circular(6) respectively, matching how BoxDecoration handles borderRadius). Cause: both lerp and scale build a new TableBorder from the six sides only, so a table with rounded corners loses them for the whole of an animation — e.g. when the table's border animates through a theme change; TableBorder.lerp(null, b, t) goes through scale, so animating a rounded border in from nothing is affected too. Reported on master and stable 3.47.8; reproduced by suryaKommana2662 and labeled "has reproducible steps"/triaged-framework. A fix is in approved PR #195398 (tests cover lerp(a,b), scale, and lerp from/to null), and ChandraChaan notes TableBorderPainter.lerp/scale (from the upcoming TableBorder deprecation in #177102) drop borderRadius the same way, so a follow-up is planned. Assigned to ChandraChaan.

Ticket #195397, "TableBorder.lerp and TableBorder.scale drop borderRadius" (open, labeled P2 Important issues not at the top of the work list; also labeled framework, has reproducible steps, team-framework, triaged-framework; assigned to ChandraChaan).

Affects master (3.50.0-1.0.pre) and stable 3.47.8.

Issue #195327 "[cupertino_ui] CupertinoListTile: add enabled" (Open, filed by @LahaLuhem). Priority is P3 ("Issues that are less important to the Flutter project"); other labels are c: proposal, p: cupertino_ui, package, team-design, triaged-design.

What is broken: CupertinoListTile has no way to render a disabled row. iOS greys out disabled list rows in both UIKit and SwiftUI, but CupertinoListTile can only drop onTap, which still leaves the row looking tappable. A null onTap can't stand in for "disabled" either, since iOS leaves rows that have nothing to tap looking unchanged.

Proposed fix (labeled c: proposal): add an `enabled` property mirroring ListTile.enabled. When false: no tap handling, title switches to tertiaryLabel color, and subtitle and additionalInfo switch to quaternaryLabel — the colors UIKit's list cells use on iOS 18.5 and 26.2. The report notes the slider has the same gap (referenced #106691).

Triage so far: suryaKommana2662 routed it to team-design, added p: cupertino_ui, team-design, c: proposal and dropped the "in triage" label; elliette added P3 and triaged-design. No assignee, type, milestone, projects, branches, or PRs.

Ticket: flutter/flutter #195468 — "[camera_android_camerax] takePicture sets an unchanged flash mode on every capture" (open, filed by @toyaji; linked fix PR flutter/packages#13468).

Priority: none — the issue's Labels section reads "No labels" (also no type, assignee, milestone, or project), so there is no priority label to report.

What is broken: In camera_android_camerax, once an app calls setFlashMode, every subsequent takePicture() re-applies the same flash mode to ImageCapture, adding roughly 250–300 ms to each capture — even when the mode is FlashMode.off and never changes. Repro: create a camera with ResolutionPreset.high, call setFlashMode(FlashMode.off) once, then call takePicture() repeatedly and measure latency. On a Galaxy S21 (SM-G991N) with camera_android_camerax 0.7.6 / CameraX 1.6.2, median of 12 shots (after 2 warm-ups, 600 ms apart): never calling setFlashMode → 517 ms (ZSL off) / 360 ms (ZSL on); calling setFlashMode(FlashMode.off) once → 794 ms / 656 ms.

Cause: takePicture calls ImageCapture.setFlashMode before every capture whenever a flash mode has been set (since flutter/packages#3800); CameraX retains the flash mode on the ImageCapture instance, so the repeat call changes nothing, but in CameraX 1.6.2 ImageCapture.setFlashMode has no unchanged-mode check, so each call still goes through CameraControl.setFlashMode (androidx-main has since added that check).

Proposed fix: only call ImageCapture.setFlashMode in takePicture when the mode differs from the one last applied to the current ImageCapture instance, keeping the torch behavior from flutter/packages#4903 (clearing a previous flash mode when torch is enabled) unchanged.
